title: Spectrum TG480RTTR Rear-Tine Petrol Cultivator — 211cc, 48cm Working Width
description_html:
The Spectrum TG480RTTR is the rear-tine cultivator to reach for when a front-tine machine has run out of muscle. With a 211cc 4-stroke OHV engine driving heavy-duty rotors through a belt-drive transmission, it's built to chew through compacted, stony or previously-uncultivated ground — the kind of conditions where lighter tillers bounce, stall or wear out.

Rear-tine layout — the engine pushes, the tines dig

Front-tine tillers rely on the operator's weight to bite into the soil. Rear-tine machines like the TG480RTTR drive forward under their own power and let the tines do the cutting independently — far less fatiguing over a long session, and the only sensible option for hard or virgin ground. The wheels do the walking; you do the steering.

211cc OHV engine built for serious workloads

The air-cooled, overhead-valve engine is the heart of the machine. OHV construction runs cooler, burns fuel more cleanly and produces lower emissions than older side-valve designs — which translates to longer service intervals and a quieter, less smoky machine in use. The 3.6-litre fuel tank keeps you working for hours between refills.

48cm working width and 20cm digging depth

A 48cm tilling width covers ground quickly without making the machine unwieldy in a domestic allotment or rear garden. The tines dig to a maximum depth of 20cm — deep enough to prepare a vegetable bed properly or break up a long-neglected lawn before re-seeding.

One forward, one reverse — easy to manoeuvre out of trouble

A two-speed gearbox with a dedicated reverse means you can back the machine out of a corner, a hedge line or a patch of unexpectedly soft ground without lifting 72kg of cultivator by hand. Pneumatic tyres on both drive wheels keep the machine steady across uneven plots.

Delivery and assembly

The TG480RTTR ships boxed for home assembly. If you'd rather have it delivered ready to run, add our Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI) service — we'll assemble, fuel-check and test the machine in our workshop before van delivery, with a short handover at the door.

title: Spectrum TG45SC Petrol Scarifier & Aerator — 223cc, 45cm, 2-in-1
description_html:
If your lawn looks tired by the back end of winter — patchy, mossy, slow to green up in spring — the problem isn't usually the grass. It's the layer of thatch and compacted soil sitting on top of it, choking out air, water and feed. The Spectrum TG45SC is built to fix exactly that, with one machine that scarifies and aerates lawns up to 2,000m².

Two jobs, one machine

The TG45SC ships with a 45cm scarifier cassette fitted as standard, with an aerator cassette included in the box. Swap cassettes by hand — no tools, no fuss — and you've got a single machine that strips moss and thatch in spring, then opens compacted soil in autumn. Buying separate scarifying and aerating machines costs the best part of a thousand pounds for a comparable specification.

223cc petrol engine, recoil start

The 223cc engine produces 6hp / 4.5kW — enough power to keep the 18 scarifier blades cutting through dense thatch without stalling. Recoil start, standard unleaded fuel, a 3.6-litre tank: nothing exotic to remember, nothing that needs a battery on charge.

Six working-height positions, from -12mm to +10mm

A single lever adjusts the cassette height across six positions. Run at -12mm for an aggressive thatch strip, +10mm to lightly tickle the surface of a newer lawn. Most users will spend their time around the middle of the range — the adjustability matters most when you're working different lawns or recovering from a bad winter.

Blade-engage clutch — leave the engine running

A green engagement lever clutches the blades in and out independently of the engine. Stop to empty the 45-litre collector, lift the machine over a path, reposition for a second pass — the engine stays running. No yanking the recoil cord a dozen times a session.

Built around a steel deck

Plastic decks warp, crack and flex under the load of a working scarifier. The TG45SC uses a pressed steel deck that holds the blade shafts in true alignment under load — the single most important thing for cassette life and cutting consistency. Foldable soft-grip handles fold down for storage, and double ball-bearing wheels push smoothly across rough ground.

A note on the clippings

Resist the temptation to throw moss and thatch on the compost heap — both can regrow. Bag them up and put them out with the green waste instead.

title: Spectrum TG45SC-E Petrol Scarifier & Aerator — 223cc, 45cm, Electric Key Start

title: Spectrum TG60FTTR Front-Tine Petrol Cultivator — 212cc, 7HP, 30/60cm Adjustable Width
description_html:
The Spectrum TG60FTTR is the front-tine cultivator we'd put in front of any allotment holder, smallholder or serious vegetable grower who needs to turn over big plots without the cost or weight of a rear-tine machine. A 212cc OHV engine, 24 hardened steel tines and a 60cm working width — adjustable down to 30cm — make short work of established beds, and the reverse gear gets you out of trouble when the ground has other ideas.

212cc OHV engine, 7HP at the tines

The air-cooled, overhead-valve engine puts out a genuine 7HP / 5.2kW and drives the tine rotors through a torque-optimised belt. OHV construction runs cooler and burns cleaner than older side-valve engines — longer-lasting, quieter, and more fuel-efficient over a working session. 3.6-litre tank.

60cm working width — drop to 30cm for tight rows

Six four-tine rotors give a full 60cm working path for fast bed preparation. Remove the outer rotor sets and the working width drops to 30cm, perfect for cultivating between established rows of vegetables, fruit canes or flower borders without damaging the crop. Most front-tine machines force you to commit to one width — the TG60FTTR lets you switch in minutes.

Adjustable depth up to 330mm

A depth-adjustable brake shoe controls how aggressively the tines dig in — from a 100mm pass for surface weeding through to a full 330mm bite for deep ploughing ahead of root crops. Heavy-duty steel construction holds the rotors true even in stony or clay-heavy ground.

Reverse gear and a front transport wheel

A dedicated reverse gear is the feature people miss most until they own a machine that has one — free yourself from a dug-in corner, back out of a hedge line or simply reposition without lifting 54kg of cultivator. A front-mounted transport wheel folds down for moving between shed and plot, then lifts clear when you're working.

Delivery and assembly

The TG60FTTR ships boxed for home assembly. If you'd rather have it delivered ready to run, add our Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI) service — we'll assemble, fuel-check and test the machine in our workshop before van delivery, with a short handover at the door.
